accent.why: Noun is stressed on the first syllable: AC-cent.

transport.why: Noun is stressed TRANS-port; trans-PORT is the verb.

update.why: Noun is stressed UP-date; up-DATE is the verb.

essay.why: Stress is on the first syllable: ES-say.

discount.why: Noun is stressed DIS-count; dis-COUNT is the verb.

superstar.why: Stress is on the first syllable: SU-per-star.

escort.why: Noun is stressed ES-cort; es-CORT is the verb.

implant.why: Noun is stressed IM-plant; im-PLANT is the verb.

ex: This car is an import from Japan.
The country's main imports are oil and gas.
Cheap imports are hurting local farmers this year.
Is this beer local or an import?
import.why: Noun is IM-port (as the note says); two examples were unnatural.

steroid.why: Stress is on the first syllable: STER-oid.

upgrade.why: Noun is stressed UP-grade; up-GRADE is the verb.

dioxide.why: Stress is on the second syllable: di-OX-ide.

lemonade.why: Main stress is on the last syllable: lem-o-NADE.

anime.why: Stress is on the first syllable: AN-i-may.

cleaning.why: клінінг is only a cleaning service; cleaning is mostly прибирання, like killer=кілер.

cheating.why: читинг is only game cheats; cheating is mostly списування, шахрайство, зрада.

OS.why: ОС is the Ukrainian abbreviation of операційна система, not a borrowing (like PC=ПК).

deacon.why: Standard Ukrainian is диякон; дякон is archaic, and ea≠я.

ex: Two plus two is four.
The room is fifty dollars plus tax.
Free parking is a big plus.
Is speaking Spanish a plus for this job?
plus.note: Also means "and also": "It's cheap, plus it's close to home."
plus.why: плюс shares the main meanings (+, and, an advantage); card showed only one.

ex: It's hard to find a balance between work and family.
What is the balance on my bank account?
A healthy diet needs a good balance of foods.
Check your balance before you pay by card.
balance.note: Also staying steady on your feet: "I lost my balance and fell."
balance.why: баланс also means equilibrium (work-life balance), not only an account balance.

ex: The museum has a manuscript from the 12th century.
Monks wrote this old manuscript by hand.
The library keeps its rare manuscripts in a cold room.
Nobody can read this ancient manuscript yet.
manuscript.note: Most often a writer's text before it is printed: "She sent her manuscript to a publisher."
manuscript.why: манускрипт is an old handwritten text; a writer's draft is рукопис.

peri.why: Rank counts pari and peri-peri; the Persian fairy sense is tiny.

jinn.why: Rank file folds 'jin' (mostly Asian names) into jinn; real jinn is rare.

olein.note: A chemistry word, seen mostly on labels of oils and soaps.
olein.why: Rank file folds 'elaine' (a name) into olein; real olein is very rare.

savanna.note: Also spelled "savannah". With a capital S, Savannah is also a US city and a girl's name.
savanna.why: Rank file folds 'Savannah' (US city, name) into savanna; grassland is ~30%.

ex: She wore a red dress a la old movie stars.
My boss wears black turtlenecks a la Steve Jobs.
He decorated his apartment a la the 1970s.
The café serves breakfast a la Paris, with croissants and coffee.
a la.why: 'a la France' is unidiomatic; replaced with a natural example.

ex: Leave your keys at the reception.
The reception is open all night.
Ask at reception for a map.
She works at reception in a big hotel.
reception.why: 'works at the reception of a hotel' is a calque; fixed.

ex: The farm is about fifty acres.
They bought ten acres of land.
The park covers two hundred acres.
One acre is about half the size of a soccer field.
acre.why: An acre is about half a soccer field, not 'a little smaller'.

policeman.say: ask a policeman · a traffic policeman
policeman.why: 'call the police' is not a collocation of policeman.

software.why: софтвер is rare jargon (VESUM slang); usual is програмне забезпечення or софт.

hardware.why: хардвер is rare jargon (VESUM slang); usual is апаратне забезпечення.

narrator.why: наратор is a rare literary term; the usual Ukrainian word is оповідач.
